meaning: `1` (Android, live) records a full barrier after every compute dispatch, as before 2026-11-09; default `0`: the barrier after a dispatch waits until other GPU work follows in the same command buffer, and a barrier recorded meanwhile (the game's) settles it, so consecutive dispatches are ordered only by the game's own barriers, as on NVN (docs/reference/rendering.md "A full barrier after every dispatch")

name: DM_VK_DISPATCH_SKIP
meaning: `=<from>[,<to>]` (Android, live) dispatches from..to of each frame (by `DM_VK_DISPATCH_LOG`'s index; default to the end) are recorded without their `vkCmdDispatch`, to find the one that writes a wrong picture

name: DM_VK_DISPATCH_SKIP_KEY
meaning: `=<hex key>[,…]` (Android, read at each dispatch) the dispatches of those compute shaders are recorded without their `vkCmdDispatch`, as `DM_VK_DISPATCH_SKIP` does by index; with the replay's `--dump-gpu` it shows what a shader writes

name: DM_VK_DISP_OBJ
meaning: `=<hex key>[,…]` or `1` (every compute shader) (Android, restart) takes each dispatch of those shaders as one object's, known by the guest addresses of the storage buffers it binds (and, a second reading, of its storage and uniform buffers), and logs every `DM_VK_DISP_OBJ_EVERY` frames per shader how many objects ran, appeared and stopped, their ages, and how many changed or zeroed the first 8 words of their first storage buffer (`dispatch objects of …`), with the game's nvnSyncWait answers and nvnQueueFinish calls in the same frames (`dispatch objects: SyncWait`), to tell objects the game keeps from objects it adds (dm/games/0400A3A01EE4C000/README.md)

name: DM_VK_DISP_OBJ_EVERY
meaning: `=<frames>` (Android, live) with `DM_VK_DISP_OBJ`, the frames between its lines (default 600)

name: DM_VK_DONE_LAST
meaning: `1` (Android, live, off) the completion thread waits for the last fence handed to the queue instead of the next one, as before (it held earlier fences back until all queued work had run); for A/B runs

name: DM_VK_DRAW
meaning: `0` / `1` (Android, live) turns draws and dispatches off or on (their records are skipped; events, counters and fences still signal); default on with placed guest memory, off without it

name: DM_VK_DRAW_SKIP_KEY
meaning: `=<hex pixel shader key>[,…]` (Android, read once) the draws of those pixel shaders are not drawn (their render pass still opens and clears), to see one pass's share of the picture, as `DM_VK_DISPATCH_SKIP_KEY` does for dispatches

name: DM_VK_DRIVER
meaning: `=<folder>` or `=<file>.so` (Android, restart) a custom Vulkan driver (a folder with a `meta.json` naming its library, loaded through libadrenotools from the app's private files); unset or `system`: the system driver; the launcher's GPU driver setting sets it, a line in `env.txt` wins

name: DM_VK_DRV_MEMO
meaning: (Android, live, on) a driver segment (c0, c2, the push bank) or the gmem table whose bytes equal the last draw's binds the same scratch span again instead of a fresh fill per draw; `0` fills one per draw

name: DM_VK_DRV_STAMP
meaning: `0` (Android, live: the next submission, 1) a graphics stage's driver segment (c0, c2, the push bank) is filled and compared with the last draw's at every draw instead of being bound again at once when nothing it is filled from changed since (`vka_draw.c` `drv_key`: the stage's storage buffer, texture / sampler / image and push constant records, base instance, sample count, pool bases)

name: DM_VK_DS_FIRST_HERE
meaning: `=0` (Android, live, default 1) a depth / stencil target's first content (its zero clear, a zero-shared image's new memory) goes through the upload batch again instead of the submission at its render pass's begin ([rendering.md](reference/rendering.md#turnip-hangs-in-the-first-3d-frame-of-a-cold-run))

name: DM_VK_DYN_FILTER
meaning: `0` / `2` (Android, live: the next submission, default 1) `1` skips dynamic state and pipeline binds equal to the last ones; `0` sets them at every draw; `2` sets them again at each pass (to bisect)

name: DM_VK_EAGER_TEX
meaning: `1` (Android, live, default 0) a texture pool slot makes and uploads its texture when the slot is written, and the image cache keeps every image a live slot names (`vka_tex.c write_tex`, `vka_tex_prune_locked`): an image for every texture the game registers (Ocarina of Time: 6,000 images, 3-4.5 GiB, killed by Android's low-memory killer in 0.2.8, issue #97); `DM_VK_POOL_FB` makes only those shaders read through the pool

name: DM_VK_ENC
meaning: `0` (Android, live: the next submission, default 1) the replay makes its `vkCmd*` calls itself instead of through the command encoder thread (`vka_enc.c`, `vk-enc`); also off while `DM_VK_GPUPROF` times a frame or `DM_VK_NANSCAN` is on

name: DM_VK_ENC_BATCH
meaning: `=<bytes>` (Android, live, 4096; at most 1 MB) the replay feeds the command encoder thread in batches of that many bytes instead of waking it for each call; `0` each call

name: DM_VK_ENC_SPIN
meaning: `=<us>` (Android, live: the next submission, 200; at most 100000) how long the command encoder thread and the replay thread wait for each other on WFE before they sleep on a futex; WFE time counts as CPU time and keeps the core out of idle

name: DM_VK_ENC_TAIL
meaning: `=<bytes>` (Android, live: the next submission, 16384; at most 1 MB) the command encoder thread tells the replay thread how far it has got (its tail: a store, a full fence and a load) every that many bytes of calls, when it has caught up and while the replay thread sleeps on it; `0` after every call, as before

name: DM_VK_EVENT_GATE
meaning: `0` (Android, restart, on) a GPU wait for an event the CPU sets parks the replay of its queue, as in v0.2.8, instead of being a gate (the replay goes on, the GPU waits for a semaphore the host signals once the word holds; `vka_qsched.h` "Waits for the CPU"); for A/B runs

name: DM_VK_EVENT_LOG
meaning: `=<n>` (Android, restart, off) logs the first n parks, gates and releases at GPU waits: the queue, the submission, the wait and the value the replay sees, whole or cut, and the submission replayed last (`vka_qsched.h`)

name: DM_VK_EVENT_PARK_MS
meaning: `=<ms>` (Android, restart, default 200) how long a queue parked at a GPU wait waits for its producer before it is released with a `[RED]` line (`vka_qsched.h`; `0`: no limit)

name: DM_VK_EVENT_WAIT
meaning: `0` (Android, restart, on) every GPU event and sync wait passes at once, as before 2026-11-09: submissions run in the order the game made them (`vka_qsched.h`); for A/B runs

name: DM_VK_FD_ALIAS
meaning: `0` (Android, restart, on) on a driver without working placed maps, the readiness check and the replay's device do not try guest memory through exported Vulkan memory (`VK_KHR_external_memory_fd`: the memory's fd mapped over the pool's range, `vka_fd_alias.h`; the readiness file says `memory.fdAlias=1` when the probe passes; draws default off without either)

name: DM_VK_FG
meaning: not read as a switch: a prefix in the Vulkan replayer's list of the live run's settings it does not take from a capture (`vka_replay.c`), which covers `DM_VK_FG_REFRESH_CAP`

name: DM_VK_FG_REFRESH_CAP
meaning: (Android, live, 1) frame generation makes no more images per game frame than the panel's refreshes in the game's period (display timing): on a 60 Hz panel a 60 fps game gets none instead of being held at 30 fps by FIFO; `0` generates the multiplier's count whatever the panel runs at (a driver whose display timing reports a refresh the panel does not run at)

name: DM_VK_FOUT_COMPS
meaning: `0` (Android, live: pixel shaders made from then on, 1) pixel shaders' colour outputs write every component of their targets, as before, instead of only the components the module stores (the others keep the target's value, as Maxwell leaves them)

name: DM_VK_FOUT_RETYPE
meaning: `=0` (Android): a pixel shader's float output into a UINT / SINT attachment is not retyped (`vka_spv_fout_retype`); that target is not written, the earlier behaviour; default on

name: DM_VK_FRAME_RATE
meaning: `0` (Android, live, 1) the window is not given the game's frame rate (`ANativeWindow_setFrameRate`, held by `DM_VK_FRAME_RATE_HOLD`); the panel's rate is left to the system

name: DM_VK_FRAME_RATE_HOLD
meaning: `=<ms>` (Android, live, 5000) the window's frame rate is the highest the game used in that time: up at once, down only after the lower rate has held that long (DKB's 60 <-> 30 switches sent the LTPO panel to 30 Hz and back, a hitch each); `0` follows every change

name: DM_VK_FSR
meaning: `1` (Android, live, off) the picture is scaled up to the window with AMD FidelityFX Super Resolution 1 (EASU, then RCAS sharpening; `vka_present.c`, `dm/third_party/fidelityfx-fsr1`) instead of the bilinear blit, when it is smaller than the window, pre-rotated or not; turns on and off from the next frame (the swapchain images always have attachment views)

name: DM_VK_FSR_SHARP
meaning: `=<stops>` (Android, live, 0.25) `DM_VK_FSR`'s RCAS sharpening in stops: 0 is the strongest, each stop halves it (AMD's scale, `FsrRcasCon`)

name: DM_VK_GATE_EVENT
meaning: `0` (Android, restart, on) a gate (a GPU wait for an event the CPU sets, `DM_VK_EVENT_GATE`) has no host event: the gated work waits only for the gate semaphore, so the CPU's writes before its signal, made after that work went to the queue, are not made visible to the GPU (`vka_dev.c` "Gates"); for A/B runs

name: DM_VK_GMEM_REACH
meaning: `=<MiB>` (Android, restart) with `DM_VK_SB_PEEK`, each 64-bit word among the first 32 of a peeked storage buffer that lies in a placed segment is taken as a pointer the shader loads (raw global memory) and it and that many MiB after it are classified as the pool table finds them (`gmem reach`: in no segment, by the 2 MiB hint, by a 6-step search of entries 0..63 as libraries built before e5c087f6 do, or only by the whole-table search)

name: DM_VK_GPL
meaning: `0` (Android, restart, on where the device has them with fast linking) graphics pipeline libraries off: a pipeline the cache lacks is made whole instead of linked from stage libraries with the optimized one made in the background

name: DM_VK_GPL_GIVEUP
meaning: `=<n>` (Android, live, 3) graphics pipeline libraries are turned off for the run after n refused pre-rasterization libraries (pipelines are then made whole)

name: DM_VK_GPL_PROBE
meaning: `1` (Android, live, off) the first refused pre-rasterization library runs a probe that makes it again with one thing changed at a time and adopts what works; a one-off diagnostic run (it makes ~11-13 libraries on the replay thread: a 1-6 s hitch)

name: DM_VK_GPUPROF
meaning: `=<n>` (Android, live, 0 = off) times one frame in n step by step with GPU timestamps between the full barriers: `gpu prof:` lines with the frame's GPU time by kind and the costliest steps (each with its pass's size and formats, its vertex / mesh / compute counts and most used shader keys), the time of mesh, vertex and dispatch steps and the dispatch time by compute shader; slows that frame a little

name: DM_VK_GPUPROF_LIST
meaning: `1` (Android, live, off) with `DM_VK_GPUPROF`, logs every step of the timed frame in order (source line, draws, ops, pass)

name: DM_VK_GPUPROF_SPLIT
meaning: `=<n>` (Android, live, 0 = off) with `DM_VK_GPUPROF`, ends each render pass of the timed frame after every n draws and opens it again (loadOp LOAD), so each step times n draws (one with n = 1): `gpu prof split:` lines give each vertex / pixel key pair and each pixel key its GPU time above the pass shape's cheapest step (the split's own load / store). The timed frame itself gets much slower

name: DM_VK_GPU_FLOOR
meaning: `=<pct>` (Android, live, default 100) the GPU clock floor: through `VK_QCOM_queue_perf_hint` in % of the highest clock (`0` the driver's governor); without it (Turnip, other drivers) through ADPF, on for any value above 0 (`DM_VK_GPU_FLOOR_ADPF`); the cost is power ([rendering.md](reference/rendering.md#gpu-end-held-back-by-recording-and-a-clocked-down-gpu-on-the-vulkan-replay), [frame-rate.md](reference/frame-rate.md#a-gpu-clock-floor-that-follows-the-present-period-holds-a-dynamic-interval-at-its-slowest))

name: DM_VK_GPU_FLOOR_ADPF
meaning: `0` (Android, live, default 1) no GPU clock floor without `VK_QCOM_queue_perf_hint`; with 1 the ADPF session reports each frame's span and GPU time against the game's shortest period ([frame-rate.md](reference/frame-rate.md#a-gpu-clock-floor-that-follows-the-present-period-holds-a-dynamic-interval-at-its-slowest))

name: DM_VK_GPU_FLOOR_AUTO
meaning: `1` / `2` (Android, live, default 0 = the fixed floor) `1`: the floor follows each frame's span (recording start to GPU end, p90 over 30 frames) against its period, in steps of 25 % between 0 and `DM_VK_GPU_FLOOR`; `2`: the floor only while a submission with draws is on the GPU, the governor otherwise

name: DM_VK_GPU_FLOOR_HI
meaning: `=<ms>` (Android, live, default 2) `DM_VK_GPU_FLOOR_AUTO=1` raises the floor a step when the span's p90 is within that many ms of the period

name: DM_VK_GPU_FLOOR_KGSL
meaning: `0` (Android, restart, default 1) no GPU clock floor through KGSL (a power constraint on the queue's kernel context, for drivers without `VK_QCOM_queue_perf_hint`: Turnip on Adreno); the ADPF floor then ([frame-rate.md](reference/frame-rate.md#a-gpu-clock-floor-that-follows-the-present-period-holds-a-dynamic-interval-at-its-slowest))

name: DM_VK_GPU_FLOOR_LO
meaning: `=<ms>` (Android, live, default 5) `DM_VK_GPU_FLOOR_AUTO=1` lowers the floor a step when the span's p90 is more than that many ms below the period (at most every 60 frames)

name: DM_VK_GPU_FLOOR_LOG
meaning: `1` / `2` (Android, live, off) `1` logs each change of the automatic GPU clock floor (frame, span p90, period); `2` also every floor the queue is given

name: DM_VK_GPU_FLOOR_PERIOD
meaning: `=<ms>` (Android, live, default 0 = the game's shortest period: the shortest present period it asked for, at most 16.7 ms) the period every GPU clock floor aims at (`DM_VK_GPU_FLOOR_AUTO=1`, the ADPF floor); `33.3` the cap before 2026-11-05

name: DM_VK_GS_CLAIM
meaning: `0` (Android, restart, on) geometry shaders' memory writes are not put under a per-primitive claim (`vka_spv_gs_claim`): they are repeated by the device's runs of each primitive

name: DM_VK_GS_LINK
meaning: `0` (Android, on) a geometry shader is not given outputs for the pixel shader's inputs it does not write (`vka_spv_gs_link`): Qualcomm's driver refuses such pipelines (-13)

name: DM_VK_GS_SPV
meaning: `=<file>` a geometry shader SPIR-V module `t_android_spvpatch` runs the memory write claim rewrite on and checks

name: DM_VK_GUEST_FPCR
meaning: `1` (Android, restart) the replay's threads and the driver's compiles (device creation, shader modules, pipelines) keep the FPCR they inherit from the game's threads (often flush-to-zero) instead of the host's (0), as before 2026-11-08: an A/B for pictures that change with it; the pipeline cache keeps no file in this mode, so expect every pipeline made again ([rendering.md](reference/rendering.md#vulkan-compiles-and-replay-threads-ran-with-the-games-flush-to-zero-fpcr-android))

name: DM_VK_GW_SORT_KEEP
meaning: `0` (Android, live, 1) the live images are sorted by storage address again at every submission start with a done GPU write into guest memory (`vka_tex_prepare`) instead of keeping the sorted list while no image comes or goes

name: DM_VK_HANG_EXIT
meaning: `0` (Android, live, 1) after a GPU hang the game runs on without the GPU instead of the host exiting

name: DM_VK_HANG_S
meaning: `=<s>` (Android, live, default 6; at least 0.5) the seconds a fence may stay unreached before a GPU hang is declared

name: DM_VK_HOOKDIR
meaning: `=<folder>` (Android, restart) where libadrenotools' hook libraries are for `DM_VK_DRIVER`; default the folder `libnxhost.so` was loaded from (inside the APK)

name: DM_VK_IMGMEM
meaning: (Android, live: images made from then on, on) images under 4 MiB that the driver does not want dedicated share 64 MiB blocks of their memory type (vka_imgmem.c, exact 256-byte units, first fit; the ctl stats' `image memory:` line); `0` gives every image its own VkDeviceMemory as before (Mario Kart World ran out of allocations that way)

name: DM_VK_IMG_LIMIT_MB
meaning: `=<MiB>` (Android, live) the texture cache's limit instead of the measured one (images plus MemAvailable less a reserve, capped by the image heap's `VK_EXT_memory_budget` share; at least 512 MiB; measured every 60 frames, the `image cache limit` line); over it images unused for 2 frames go, least recently used first, and the cache stays over the limit rather than evict a recent one ([memory.md](reference/memory.md#texture-cache-thrash-at-a-fixed-image-limit-android))

name: DM_VK_IMG_RETYPE
meaning: `0` (Android, live: the next dispatch, on) a compute shader's float storage images bound to integer textures (an R32_UINT view of an RGB9E5 target) keep the float view of the same size (vka_tex.c class_twin) instead of a pipeline whose module types them as the texture's class (vka_spv_img_retype; docs/reference/shaders.md)

name: DM_VK_IMG_SPV
meaning: `=<file>:<binding>[,…]` SPIR-V modules and the set 0 binding of a float storage image in each that `t_android_spvpatch` retypes as uint and as int (vka_spv_img_retype) and checks

name: DM_VK_IMG_UPGRADE
meaning: `0` (Android, live: the next binding, on) a texture bound as a shader image without NVN's IMAGE flag is no longer remade with storage use, and an image registration no longer counts as image intent

name: DM_VK_INSTANCE
meaning: `1` (Android, live, off; Game settings › Instanced draws) runs of direct indexed draws that repeat one mesh and move only one vertex and one pixel uniform block by the same amount are drawn as one instanced draw with instanced shader variants

name: DM_VK_INSTANCE_FAST
meaning: `0` (Android, with `DM_VK_INSTANCE`, default 1) a draw joins an instanced run only through the full path (the descriptor walk), never by the fast comparison of its uniform slots

name: DM_VK_LC_GLOBAL
meaning: (Android, restart, on) the recording thread's address lookup cache lives in a global the first recording thread owns, not in TLS (a dlopen'ed library's `__thread` access goes through the TLS resolver: 8 % of the replay thread); `0` TLS for every thread

name: DM_VK_LOG
meaning: `=1` logs Vulkan object creation in the Vulkan-on-Metal layer

name: DM_VK_MAPS
meaning: `0` (Android, restart, on) the memory maps thread is not started: no count of /proc/self/maps, no `memory maps:` lines, no coarser write-protection blocks near vm.max_map_count, no compaction

name: DM_VK_MAPS_BUDGET
meaning: `=<percent>` (Android, default 75) the share of vm.max_map_count from which placed segments split by write protection get their CPU map made again in one piece (down to 55 %)

name: DM_VK_MAPS_CACHE
meaning: (Android, on) placing and giving back memory pools take the page protections from a snapshot of /proc/self/maps, read again only for a range whose 256 KiB blocks changed since (this library's mmap / munmap / mprotect / mremap mark them; a pool swap marks its range only when it may not have put the protections back); answers from the snapshot are checked against the text (the first 16, then every 64th). `0` reads the text each time (1-5 ms a pool on the phone)

name: DM_VK_MAPS_COMPACT
meaning: `0` (Android, on) placed segments are not compacted past `DM_VK_MAPS_BUDGET` (the dirty tracker's blocks still get coarser as the count climbs)

name: DM_VK_MAPS_COMPACT_N
meaning: `=<n>` (Android, default 8, at most 256) placed segments compacted in one round (a round at most every 20 s)

name: DM_VK_MAPS_HIST
meaning: `=<percent>` (Android, default 40, `0` off) from this share of vm.max_map_count the memory maps thread logs the 10 largest groups of maps outside the guest block by (name with digits folded to `#`, permissions, size bucket): when the count climbs past it, at each further 10 % and every 30 s while it stays over (`memory maps outside the guest block:` lines)

name: DM_VK_MAPS_PERIOD_S
meaning: `=<s>` (Android, default 5) seconds between two counts of the process's memory maps

name: DM_VK_MDI_GPU
meaning: `0` (Android, live, on) reads an indirect-count multi-draw's count on the CPU while recording and makes each record a draw of its own, as before, instead of one `vkCmdDraw*IndirectCount` at its first record with the count read by the GPU ([rendering.md](reference/rendering.md#indirect-count-multi-draws-counted-on-the-cpu-on-the-vulkan-replay))

name: DM_VK_MEMLOG
meaning: `=<MiB>` (Android, default 512, `0` off): a `memory:` log line each time the replay's placed pools, images and scratch memory have taken that much more (allocations counted, frees not) since the last line

name: DM_VK_MEM_LOCK_WHOLE
meaning: `1` (Android, restart): a memory pool placement holds the segment table's write lock for its whole duration, as before 2026-11-03 (the replay and the game's NVN calls wait for it: DKB's 300-500 ms loading hitches); for A/B only

name: DM_VK_MESH
meaning: `0` (Android, restart, on) leaves VK_EXT_mesh_shader off: NVN2 task and mesh shaders are refused and their draws (nvnCommandBufferDrawMeshTasks) skipped, as on a device without the task and mesh stages

name: DM_VK_MESH_IND
meaning: `0` (Android, live, on) draws an indirect mesh draw from its NVN2 record itself (x = count, y = first workgroup: nothing drawn) instead of a {count, 1, 1} copy made on the GPU before the pass ([rendering.md](reference/rendering.md#indirect-mesh-draws-drew-nothing))

name: DM_VK_MESH_LOG
meaning: `1` (Android) logs each task / mesh / pixel shader triple of a mesh draw once, with its first draw's workgroup count and whether the mesh shader has per-primitive outputs

name: DM_VK_MESH_PREPASS_SKIP
meaning: `0` / `1` (Android, live; unset: on with Qualcomm's driver) the profile's `mesh_prepass_cut` workaround: `0` draws the listed depth-only mesh prepass draws and keeps their colour pass's EQUAL, `1` skips and relaxes them on every driver ([rendering.md](reference/rendering.md#depth-only-mesh-prepass-drawn-as-spikes-on-qualcomms-driver))

name: DM_VK_MESH_SKIP
meaning: `=<mesh key>,...` (Android) skips the mesh draws of those mesh shaders, to find a wrong mesh draw by taking draws away in a replay

name: DM_VK_NANSCAN
meaning: `1` / `2` (Android, restart, needs push descriptors) after every render pass scans the float colour attachments (and the float storage images each dispatch wrote) for NaN / infinite texels and logs the passes with any (frame, attachment, shaders); `2` also splits passes to find the draw (`DM_VK_NANSCAN_STEP`, `_DRAWS`, `_SERIAL`); not for play

name: DM_VK_NANSCAN_BIG
meaning: `=<value>` (Android, restart) with `DM_VK_NANSCAN`, finite texels with a channel above that value (absolute) count as infinite: to find the pass or draw that first writes out-of-range values (fireflies that bloom spreads)

name: DM_VK_NANSCAN_DRAWS
meaning: `=<from>-<to>` (Android, restart) with `DM_VK_NANSCAN=2`, split only the game's passes whose index is in that range (default all)

name: DM_VK_NANSCAN_DUMP
meaning: `=<format>x<width>` (Android, live: read at use) with `DM_VK_NANSCAN`, writes level 0 of ASTC textures of that format (hex) and width to `DM_TEMP` (`nan-<serial>-<format>-<w>x<h>.blk`, at most 64); set at all, also dumps the ASTC textures a NaN pass's draws sample

name: DM_VK_NANSCAN_FROM
meaning: `=<frame>` (Android, restart) with `DM_VK_NANSCAN`, scans the passes only from that frame on, so the 200 logged lines are not spent on the title and menus

name: DM_VK_NANSCAN_FS
meaning: `=<key>` (Android, restart) with `DM_VK_NANSCAN`, a fragment shader key (hex) whose draw, once a frame, has its inputs scanned for NaN / infinite texels

name: DM_VK_NANSCAN_LINES
meaning: `=<n>` (Android, restart) with `DM_VK_NANSCAN`, the most result lines logged in a run (default 200)

name: DM_VK_NANSCAN_SERIAL
meaning: `=<serial>` (Android, restart) with `DM_VK_NANSCAN=2`, split only passes into the image of that texture serial (default any)

name: DM_VK_NANSCAN_STEP
meaning: `=<n>` (Android, restart, default 64) with `DM_VK_NANSCAN=2`, the pass is ended and scanned after every n draws

name: DM_VK_NDSR
meaning: `=<n>` (Android, live, default 4 since 2026-11-10: FSR 1's picture is too bright on Qualcomm's driver in Ocarina of Time, open) what runs in place of a game's neural upscaler (agl's NDSR network: Donkey Kong Bananza, Ocarina of Time's light upscaler): `0` the game's own network, `1` a smooth stretch, `2` FSR 1, `3` nearest neighbor, `4` Qualcomm's SGSR 1 (one pass, its own sharpening); the launcher sets it from the Upscaler setting, the in-game panel while the game runs. A change takes the network's next dispatch in every direction (`0` included: the network's pipeline is made at its first dispatch whatever the mode) and is logged once: `NDSR upscaler: DM_VK_NDSR=<n> (<name>) from network <key>'s next dispatch on (a live change)`

name: DM_VK_NDSR_INPUT
meaning: `linear` / `sqrt` (Android, live; default: by the input's format, B10G11R11 the colour, E5B9G9R9 sqrt(colour) as agl's light upscaler packs it) what the NDSR network's input holds when `DM_VK_NDSR` replaces it; `sqrt` squares the result

name: DM_VK_NDSR_SHARP
meaning: `=<stops>` (Android, live, default 0.25) how much FSR sharpens after scaling up in place of the neural upscaler: `0` the most, each stop halves it, below 0 no sharpening

name: DM_VK_OCCLUSION
meaning: `0` (Android, read once at the first samples-passed reset or report) samples-passed reports are not counted with Vulkan occlusion queries: every one writes 1, as before 2026-11-08 (the A/B for the counted occlusion queries)

name: DM_VK_OVERLAY
meaning: `0` (Android, live, 1) the launcher's overlay (build tag, frame rate and its items) is shown by Android views over the game instead of being drawn by the present into the game's images (`vka_present.c` `ovl_draw`; the views made the app's window draw and the compositor blend a second changing layer, issue #34)

name: DM_VK_PACE_LOG
meaning: `=<ms>` (Android, live, 5000) a `[vk] pace` line every that many ms: intervals, fps, GPU busy and span p50/p90, the replay's recording and its CPU time, draws, GPU clock floor, ADPF mode, window rate and panel refresh, thermal status and headroom, CPU clocks; `0` off; and a `[vk] pace cost` line: the recording split into draws, texture prepare, submission start, commit and other records, the replay and encoder threads' time on a core, waiting for one and their switches, the encoder's time by kind of call, the draw path by phase (`DM_VK_PACE_PROF`)

name: DM_VK_PACE_PROF
meaning: `=<n>` (Android, live: the next submission, 16) with `DM_VK_PACE_LOG`, one draw in n is timed by phase for the `[vk] pace cost` line (ten counter reads in such a draw); `0` none (the line then has no draw path part); `DM_VK_PROF=1` times every draw

name: DM_VK_PARTLOG
meaning: `1` (Android, live, off) one line for each part a submission goes to the queue in (its draws, when it ended) and for each part the GPU finished (its GPU time), read without waiting while the submission is recorded; passes split inside are named, and each part's line gives the depth state of its draws into depth targets (test, write, compare ops, direction flips, writes with ALWAYS / NOT_EQUAL, stencil, bias, discard, clears inside a pass, passes begun, kept game barriers, timestamps inside a pass) ([rendering.md](reference/rendering.md#turnip-hangs-in-the-first-3d-frame-of-a-cold-run))

name: DM_VK_PASS_CLEARS
meaning: `0` (Android, live: the next submission, 1) clears of the bound targets are made outside the render pass instead of inside the pass over them (each such clear then ends the pass)

name: DM_VK_PASS_KEEP
meaning: `0` (Android, live: the next submission, 1) a render target change ends the open pass at once instead of only when the next draw's targets differ

name: DM_VK_PCACHE
meaning: `=<file>` (Android, restart) the Vulkan pipeline cache file; `0` no file; default `$DM_TEMP/vk_pipelines-fp0.bin` (`vk_pipelines-<driver>-fp0.bin` with a custom driver; `-fp0` is the cache's generation, and the files without one, compiled with the game's FPCR, are removed); the replayer does not take it from a capture. Its stamp `<file>.lib` (written with each save) names the shader library it was saved with and lists its shaders; a file of another library is read while `DM_VK_PCACHE_KEEP` allows ([memory.md](reference/memory.md#a-shader-library-update-that-threw-the-pipeline-cache-away-android))

name: DM_VK_PCACHE_KEEP
meaning: `=<percent>` (Android, restart, 50) a pipeline cache file of another shader library is read while the shaders it holds that the new library changed or dropped (counted over every update it was kept across) are at most this percent of those still the same; else the run starts empty. `0` never reads another library's file ([memory.md](reference/memory.md#a-shader-library-update-that-threw-the-pipeline-cache-away-android))

name: DM_VK_PCACHE_SAVE_S
meaning: `=<s>` (Android, live, 20; at least 1) the pipeline cache file is saved at most every s seconds while new pipelines are made, checked at each submission and after a pipeline that took over 1 s on the frame path (the save at the end of the run and at suspend is forced)

name: DM_VK_PCACHE_SAVE_SLOW_S
meaning: `=<s>` (Android, live, 3; at least 1) after a pipeline that took over 1 s on the frame path, the pipeline cache file is saved when its last save is at least s seconds old (on the saver thread), so a slow pipeline made just before the process is stopped or killed is kept

name: DM_VK_PFB_SPV_DIR
meaning: `=<folder>` (`dm/host/tests/t_android_spvpatch.c`) each `.spv` module there that reads the texture pool rewritten by `vka_spv_pool_fb` and validated

name: DM_VK_PICTURE_SIZE
meaning: `=<percent>` (Android, live, 100; 50 to 100) the game's picture is drawn at that share of its fitted (or, with `DM_VK_STRETCH`, stretched) size, its shape kept, with black around it, placed by the picture position (`vka_present_fit.h`); the in-game panel's Picture › Size sets it, per game, and maps touches to the same rectangle

name: DM_VK_PLACED
meaning: `0` (Android, restart, on) memory pools stay anonymous memory instead of placed Vulkan memory, so the GPU sees none (draws then default off, `DM_VK_DRAW`)

name: DM_VK_PLACED_PROBE
meaning: `0` (Android, restart, on) on a driver that lists neither VK_EXT_map_memory_placed nor VK_KHR_map_memory2, the readiness check and the replay's device do not try one placed map of a test allocation to find placed maps that work without being advertised (the readiness file then says `placed.unadvertised=1`)

name: DM_VK_PLACE_GRANULE_MB
meaning: `=<MB>` (Android, read once, 16) the part size of a memory pool placed by parts (`DM_VK_PLACE_PART_MB`): only the parts the GPU is given an address in become placed memory ([memory.md](reference/memory.md))

name: DM_VK_PLACE_JOIN_MB
meaning: `=<MB>` (Android, read once, 256; `0` no joins) the largest run of parts of a memory pool placed by parts that a range given to the GPU lies across, joined into one at the next submission ([memory.md](reference/memory.md#a-range-given-to-the-gpu-across-two-placed-parts-of-a-pool-android))

name: DM_VK_PLACE_LAZY
meaning: `0` (Android, read once, on) every memory pool is placed when it is made, instead of when the GPU is first given an address in it ([memory.md](reference/memory.md))

name: DM_VK_PLACE_PART_MB
meaning: `=<MB>` (Android, read once, 1024; `0` whole pools, as before) memory pools of at least this size are placed by parts of `DM_VK_PLACE_GRANULE_MB` instead of whole ([memory.md](reference/memory.md))

name: DM_VK_PLACE_SHADER_POOLS
meaning: `1` (Android, read once, default 0 for every game) NVN SHADER_CODE memory pools are placed for their address and buffer objects over them again, as before; by default one is placed only for a recorded command naming an address in it (binds, draws, copies, clears, reports, conditional render), a texture over it or a virtual-pool mapping of it, since the Vulkan replay never hands the GPU shader code (the host hashes it on the CPU, `nvn_shader_code_readable`); the way back if a game reads data in such a pool through a raw pointer (`hle_nvn.c` "Shader-code pools", [memory.md](reference/memory.md#shader-code-pools-placed-though-the-gpu-never-reads-them-android); from Anka Native)

name: DM_VK_POOL_FB
meaning: `0` (Android, restart, default 1) the GPU no longer reports the texture IDs shaders read through the texture pool: every module made gets code that sets a bit per ID it reads there (`vka_spvpatch.c vka_spv_pool_fb`, a bitmap at set 2 binding 0), read back after each submission (`vka_tex.c` "Texture pool reads"), so a texture read only through the pool is made when first read and kept while read; with `0` such a texture reads zeros, as in 0.2.2-0.2.7 ([rendering.md](reference/rendering.md#textures-read-only-through-the-pool-were-never-made-android))

name: DM_VK_POOL_FB_EARLY
meaning: `0` (Android, read when a module is made, default 1) no pixel module that reports its pool reads gets EarlyFragmentTests; its depth and stencil tests then run after shading (its stores would otherwise run for fragments the test kills), slower where the test culls much

name: DM_VK_POOL_SLOT_BIND
meaning: `1` (Android, live, off) a direct texture or image binding writes its own view (its shape and class) into the pool table's slot, as before 2026-11-10; by default a slot holds the texture's own view and is written only when that changes (`vka_tex.c` "What each slot of the pool tables holds"): an A/B for Mario Kart World's lost device with GPU waits on

name: DM_VK_PREFAULT
meaning: `0` (Android, restart, on) placed maps are not faulted in after placing; a diagnostic to measure whether the driver needs it

name: DM_VK_PRESENT_NEAREST
meaning: `1` (Android, live, off) the picture is scaled to the window with nearest neighbor instead of smooth filtering; the launcher's Upscaler setting "Nearest neighbor" sets it

name: DM_VK_PRESENT_PREWAIT
meaning: `0` (Android, live, on) the present thread does not wait on the CPU for the frame before it takes the queue lock (as before; for A/B runs)

name: DM_VK_PRETRANSFORM
meaning: `0` (Android, live: makes a new swapchain, 1) no pre-rotation: the compositor rotates the picture instead of it being drawn in the panel's own orientation

name: DM_VK_PREWARM
meaning: `=<n>` (Android, restart, 4; at most 4) threads that make the prewarm list's pipelines (`vk_pipelines.keys`, the keys of earlier runs) in the background at nice 10 when the first pipeline is made; `0` off. The replay tool sets it to 0

name: DM_VK_PREWARM_FILE
meaning: `=<file>` (Android, restart) the prewarm list's path; default `<DM_VK_PCACHE file>.keys`, else `$DM_TEMP/vk_pipelines.keys`

name: DM_VK_PREWARM_HEAVY_MS
meaning: `=<ms>` (Android, restart, 1000; `0` never) a prewarm thread holds its next compile while any pipeline build in the process has run this long, or while another build of the same vertex, mesh or compute shader runs, and a shader an earlier build found that long (kept in `<pipeline cache>.heavy`) while another such one builds: Turnip keeps thousands of 64 KiB-1 MiB blocks for a multi-second compile, each mapped apart by the allocator, and three at once took Ocarina of Time past vm.max_map_count

name: DM_VK_PREWARM_KEEP
meaning: `=<n>` (Android, live: the next write, 16384; `0` no limit) the prewarm list keeps at most the newest n records when written; the oldest loaded keys (ones no recent run needed) go first

name: DM_VK_PREWARM_MAX
meaning: `=<n>` (Android, restart, 8192) the prewarm threads make at most n pipelines of the list

name: DM_VK_PREWARM_MEM_MB
meaning: `=<MiB>` (Android, restart, 2048; `0` never) every prewarm thread but the first waits while the phone's MemAvailable is under this: compiles take the driver hundreds of MB each, and four at once with the first 3D scene loaded ran a phone out of memory

name: DM_VK_PREWARM_OVERLAP
meaning: `1` (Android, restart; default 0 on Turnip, 1 on other drivers, by `driverID`) each prewarm thread builds on its own, as before; `0` one prewarm build runs at a time (the threads still prepare their keys in parallel), since a build's cost is known only after it and four long Turnip compiles that started within one second took Ocarina of Time past vm.max_map_count. Qualcomm's driver's compiler does not take the maps with it

name: DM_VK_PREWARM_SEED
meaning: `0` (Android, restart, 1) leaves the profile's seed list (`dm/games/<id>/vk_prewarm.bin`, compiled into the host) out of the prewarm list: a first start then makes ahead only what earlier runs on this device made

name: DM_VK_PREWARM_WHY
meaning: `=<n>` (Android, 64; `0` none): for the first n pipelines the frame path makes, a log line saying why the prewarm list did not have them (no record with their shaders, or the fields in which the nearest record differs)

name: DM_VK_PROF
meaning: `1` (Android, live: the next submission, off) times the draw recording path's steps (resolve, layout, pipeline, sets, vertex buffers, draw; set writes and pushes) per draw and adds them to the replay statistics line

name: DM_VK_PSO_ASYNC
meaning: `=<n>` (Android, restart, 0; at most 4) threads that make the graphics pipelines the frame path misses (a cache-only try still runs on the frame path), their draws skipped until made, so a new pipeline costs no frame wait; `0` off: the frame waits for it. Compute and mesh pipelines stay on the frame path. With GPL off (a driver that refuses libraries, as Qualcomm's on the Adreno 840) there is no cache-only try, so a pipeline the pipeline cache already holds is made in the background too and its draws skipped for a moment. The threads run at nice 10

name: DM_VK_PUSH_DEDUP
meaning: `0` (Android, live, 1) a push descriptor update equal to the last one of its bind point is pushed again instead of skipped

name: DM_VK_PUSH_DELTA
meaning: `1` (Android, live, off) push descriptor updates write only the descriptors that changed since the last push of the same set; off until phone-checked (a driver that mishandles incremental pushes shows wrong textures)

name: DM_VK_QS_TRACE
meaning: `=<n>` (Android, restart, default 512; `0` off) keeps the last n events of the GPU-wait scheduler and the submissions (each submission taken, park, wait that held at once with the value it saw and its source, release, valve, replayed event signal, commit with its timeline signal, part split, event value the completion thread wrote, present, CPU fence wait, failed submit) and prints them oldest first when a GPU hang is declared (`vka_worker.c` "The GPU-wait trace"); nothing is logged otherwise

name: DM_VK_RANGE_WATCH
meaning: `=<hex addr>[+<hex bytes>]` (Android, restart; default 16 bytes, at most 64) finds who writes those guest bytes whatever the path (a storage binding, a store through a loaded address, a copy, a fill, inline data): the GPU copies them before a submission's first dispatch or transfer and after each one, and each step that changed them is logged with its shader key or transfer (`range watch`), then what the CPU reads once the submission is done; draws show at the next step or the submission's end

name: DM_VK_RANGE_WATCH_FRAMES
meaning: `=<n>` (Android, live) with `DM_VK_RANGE_WATCH`, how many frames are followed (default 3); each step costs a copy and a barrier

name: DM_VK_RANGE_WATCH_FROM
meaning: `=<frame>` (Android, live) with `DM_VK_RANGE_WATCH`, the first frame followed (default 0)

name: DM_VK_RANGE_WATCH_LINES
meaning: `=<n>` (Android, live) with `DM_VK_RANGE_WATCH`, the most lines logged in a run (default 400)

name: DM_VK_RC_LOG
meaning: `=<lines>` (Android, restart; with the profile key `render_cond`) logs render conditions as the replay decides them (`rc` lines): counter resets and query reports, each condition with the two counters memory holds at record time and the last report posted to each address (this submission, written, or `PENDING`: memory is older than that report), what each conditional block ran or skipped (draws with their first keys, clears with their targets), and every clear of a 3D colour target (slices, in the pass or outside)

name: DM_VK_RC_LOG_FROM
meaning: `=<frame>` (Android, live) with `DM_VK_RC_LOG`, logs only from that frame on (reports before it are still recorded for the `rc cond` lines)

name: DM_VK_RC_QUERY_MEM
meaning: `1` (Android, live) a render condition on a report the replay writes as a constant, or on a counted samples-passed report still in flight, reads memory instead of drawing as unknown (as before the report table): an A/B against the default

name: DM_VK_READTEXELS
meaning: `0` (Android, live, 1) the game's CPU texel reads (`nvnTextureReadTexels`) leave its destination unwritten, as before (`vka_tex.c` `mtl_read_texels`); by default they copy the texels from the guest storage, or from the Vulkan image when the GPU wrote the texture

name: DM_VK_REPLAY_NICE
meaning: `=<nice>` (Android, live: the next submission, -8; -20..19) the replay thread's priority, as the command encoder's and the completion thread's; `0` leaves it as the thread was made (as before: the priority of the game thread that started it, -4 for a guest thread)

name: DM_VK_ROWS
meaning: `0` (Android, live: the next re-upload, 1) a tracked linear 2D texture whose storage the CPU wrote is re-uploaded whole instead of only the rows between the written bytes

name: DM_VK_RT_LOG
meaning: `=<w>x<h>` (Android, live) every render pass of that size logs its begin (`rt log pass`: targets, load ops, clear values, late clears) and each draw in it (`rt log draw`: shaders, primitive, counts, instances, indirect record, cull and front face as NVN set them and as drawn, depth test / write / op / clamp, stencil, rasterizer discard, alpha test, viewport, scissor, each target's write mask, the shader's written components and blend; then attribute 0's format and stream and, for a direct draw of 16- or 32-bit floats, indexed or not, the extent of the vertices of its first 256 vertices or indices and the first two raw); draws into such targets that a render condition skips or that end early (empty scissor, both faces culled, past a multi-draw's count) get a line too: to see why a small pass leaves its target as cleared

name: DM_VK_RT_LOG_LINES
meaning: `=<n>` (Android, live) with `DM_VK_RT_LOG`, the most lines in a run (default 400; only logged lines count, so raising it later logs more)

name: DM_VK_SB_PEEK
meaning: `=<hex key>[,…]` (Android, restart) logs the storage buffers those shaders bind (draws and dispatches): their address and first words as the CPU sees them when the draw or dispatch is recorded (`sb peek recorded`) and again when its submission has completed (`sb peek done`), to follow sums a shader leaves for the CPU

name: DM_VK_SB_PEEK_AT
meaning: `=<word>[,<word>…]` (Android, live) with `DM_VK_SB_PEEK`, the first of the 8 words each line shows (default 0; the first 64 words of a buffer are read); a list (at most 8) logs one line per window, each counted in `DM_VK_SB_PEEK_LINES`

name: DM_VK_SB_PEEK_FROM
meaning: `=<frame>` (Android, live) with `DM_VK_SB_PEEK`, logs only from that frame on, so the lines are not spent on the first frames that run those shaders

name: DM_VK_SB_PEEK_LINES
meaning: `=<n>` (Android, live) with `DM_VK_SB_PEEK`, the most lines logged in a run (default 200); only logged lines count, so raising it later logs more

name: DM_VK_SB_WATCH
meaning: `1` (Android, live) with `DM_VK_SB_PEEK`, watches the storage buffers the peeked shaders may write and logs once each other shader's uniform or storage buffer binding over them (`sb watch`: shader, stage, binding, storage or uniform, a uniform buffer bound in place or as a copy of the CPU's bytes), to find who reads what they leave; reads through raw global memory are not seen

name: DM_VK_SHARED_SPILL_MB
meaning: `=<MiB>` (Android, default 16): the shared memory spill buffer of compute programs over the device's shared memory (`vka_draw.c` `spill_buf`); a dispatch with more workgroups than its slices runs in parts

name: DM_VK_SHLIB
meaning: `=<file>` (Android, restart) the Vulkan shader library to load; default `<module dir>/shaders/<Vulkan chain dir>/<library file>`; the replayer does not take it from a capture; `t_android_shlib` reads it for its real-library test

name: DM_VK_SHLIB_ALL
meaning: set: `t_android_shlib` checks every entry of the real library (`DM_VK_SHLIB`) instead of a sample (every 97th plus geometry, compute, task, mesh)

name: DM_VK_SHLIB_CHECK
meaning: `1` (Android, restart) when the shader library loads, builds every shader module and compute pipeline of it and logs a `shader library check:` line (made, refused, without a layout, failed)

name: DM_VK_SHPOOL_LOG
meaning: `1` (Android, read once, off) logs each NVN SHADER_CODE pool's uses once per pool and kind (its address, buffer objects, textures, each kind of command naming an address in it) and whether it is placed for them, and a `[nvn] shader-code pools at present` summary at presents 60, 300 and every 1800 (`hle_nvn.c` "Shader-code pools"; from Anka Native)

name: DM_VK_SHUFFLE_LDS
meaning: `0` / `1` (Android, restart; default 1 on Turnip, 0 elsewhere) compute shaders take their `DMSH_VK_MOD_SHUFFLE_LDS` module (32-bit subgroup shuffles through workgroup memory) where the library has one; `0` the shuffle instruction ([shaders.md](reference/shaders.md#ampere-hmma-and-warp-shuffles-of-agls-upscaler-on-adreno))

name: DM_VK_SKIP_NDVE
meaning: `0` runs the NDVE compute shaders the Vulkan replay skips by default (`vka_is_ndve_key`, `vka_draw.c`, `vka_pso.c`)

name: DM_VK_SPARSE_DENSE_MB
meaning: `=<MiB>` (Android, live: images made from now on, default 128; `0` no cap): a sampled sparse-pool texture with no sparse residency image (its format has none, as no block-compressed format on the Adreno 840) is a dense image from the finest level whose levels take at most this much; its finer levels are left out (`vka_tex.c` `dense_floor`)

name: DM_VK_SPARSE_LEVELS
meaning: `=0` (Android, on by default) makes every sampled texture of a sparse pool an image at its full size, as before, instead of an image of only the levels where pages are mapped

name: DM_VK_SPARSE_RES
meaning: `=0` (Android, on when the device has sparse residency for 2D images) makes large sampled textures of sparse pools dense images again instead of sparse residency images bound tile by tile as the page table maps them (`dm/gfx/vk_android/vka_sparse.c`); read once

name: DM_VK_SPARSE_RES_MB
meaning: `=<MiB>` (Android, default 32): the size from which a sampled sparse-pool texture's image (from its base level) is a sparse residency image; smaller ones stay dense

name: DM_VK_SPEC_FOLD
meaning: `0` (Android, restart, on) leaves task and mesh shaders' specialization constants as they are (a VkSpecializationInfo) instead of folding them into their modules; on Qualcomm's driver their subgroup lanes then read as 0 (it reads them so in a module with a specialization constant), which puts mesh vertices in the wrong slots (docs/reference/shaders.md)

name: DM_VK_SPV_DIR
meaning: `=<dir>` `t_android_spvpatch` runs the vertex input retype rewrite on every `.spv` module there and checks them

name: DM_VK_STATS
meaning: `0` (Android, live, 1) no `replay up to frame` statistics lines every 300 frames; the replayer sets it to 0

name: DM_VK_STORAGE_FIRST_USE
meaning: `=0` (Android, Switch 2 games): an uncompressed texture first used as a sampled texture ID is not taken from its storage (cleared instead, the earlier behaviour); default on (`vka_tex.c` `nvn2_sampled_content`)

name: DM_VK_STRETCH
meaning: `1` (Android, live, off) the game's picture is stretched over the whole window instead of fitted with its aspect ratio kept (`vka_present_fit.h`); Game settings › Display › Stretch to screen and the in-game panel's Picture › Fit / Stretch set it, per game; the panel's change reaches the running game through `DM_CTL` and the launcher maps touches to the same rectangle

name: DM_VK_SUBGROUP_GS
meaning: `0` / `1` (Android, restart) `0`: the geometry stage runs one-lane subgroups; `1`: as the device reports; default 0 on Turnip (which computes subgroup operations wrong there), 1 on other drivers

name: DM_VK_SUBGROUP_PIN
meaning: `=<stage mask>` (Android, restart, default 1 = every stage that can) the stages (`VkShaderStageFlags`) whose subgroup size is pinned to the shader library's; `0` none

name: DM_VK_SWAP_RB
meaning: `=<n>` the present's red/blue swap (`vka_present.c vka_swap_rb`; default the profile's `DM_GAME_SWAP_RB`, else 0)

name: DM_VK_SYNCLOG
meaning: `=<n>` (Android, live, 0 = off) logs the game's next n waits together with each submission's recording and queueing times and timestamp reports (`sync …` lines, one clock in ms)

name: DM_VK_TEST_HANG
meaning: `=<mode>[,<ticket>]` (Android, restart; ticket default 600) at that present the copy waits for a timeline value no earlier batch signals: mode 1 the next fence, mode 2 a value nothing signals (a sure stall, to test the hang handling)

name: DM_VK_TEX_MEMO
meaning: `0` (Android, live, 1) the recording thread looks every texture and sampler ID up again instead of reusing its memo of the last view for that ID

name: DM_VK_TEX_PEEK
meaning: `=<hex key>[,…]` or `=all` (Android, restart) logs each texture and shader-image binding of those shaders' draws and dispatches (`tex peek`: texture ID, what it stands for, its storage address, the image it is drawn from and whether a view was made) and the colour and depth targets of every render pass that opens (`rt peek`), to follow which textures share an image

name: DM_VK_TEX_PEEK_FROM
meaning: `=<frame>` (Android, live) with `DM_VK_TEX_PEEK`, logs only from that frame on

name: DM_VK_TEX_PEEK_LINES
meaning: `=<n>` (Android, live) with `DM_VK_TEX_PEEK`, the most lines logged in a run (default 400)

name: DM_VK_TEX_RETYPE
meaning: `0` (Android, live: the next draw, on) a graphics stage's float textures and images bound to texture views of an integer format (R16G16_UINT, R32_UINT, RGBA8_UINT) are read through float views of the same size (vka_tex.c class_twin), which convert the integers, instead of a pipeline whose stage module types them as the view's class (vka_draw.c tex_masks, vka_shader_tex_module; docs/reference/shaders.md)

name: DM_VK_TEX_SOFT
meaning: `0` / `1` (Android, live: images made from then on) overrides the profile's `tex_soft`: large block-compressed textures from the game's files kept without their finest level (`dm/gfx/vk_android/vka_tex.c` "Soft textures"; the ctl stats' `soft textures:` line counts them)

name: DM_VK_TEX_SPV
meaning: `=<file>:<binding>[,…]` SPIR-V modules and the set 0 binding of a float texture (combined image and sampler, or sampled image) in each that `t_android_spvpatch` retypes as uint and as int (vka_spv_img_retype) and checks

name: DM_VK_TEX_STATS
meaning: `=<fragment shader key>[,…]` (Android, live) the first draw of each frame with one of those fragment shaders has level 0 of each sampled texture (each layer up to 6, a 3D texture whole) scanned before it, and one `tex stats:` line per texture and layer logs, per channel, the share of texels with |c| > 1/1024 and the largest |c| (and the binding, texture ID, serial, format, size), after one `tex stats: fragment <key> input binding …` line describing each texture (once for each fragment shader, binding and texture ID, outside the line budget): to find which input of a lit material is zero; the encoder thread is off while it is set; a new value starts again; not for play

name: DM_VK_TEX_STATS_DRAWS
meaning: `=<n>` (Android, live) with `DM_VK_TEX_STATS`, the first n draws of each frame with one of its fragment shaders are scanned (default 1); each texture is scanned once a frame

name: DM_VK_TEX_STATS_LINES
meaning: `=<n>` (Android, live) with `DM_VK_TEX_STATS`, the most `tex stats:` value lines logged for one value of it (default 200; only logged lines count, so raising it later logs more); no scans once they are spent

name: DM_VK_TEX_STATS_TABLE
meaning: `=<sb>,<base ub>:<word>,<bias ub>:<word>,<index ub>:<word>[/<word>…],<offset>[/<offset>…]` (Android, live) with `DM_VK_TEX_STATS`, also the bindless textures each scanned draw reads through a record table of handles in a storage buffer (agl / gsys lit materials: lightmaps, baked occlusion): one `tex stats table:` line per draw and index word with the record's words and handles, then those textures' `tex stats` lines (binding 1000 + 100 × index + offset). Format in `dm/gfx/vk_android/vka_nanscan.c`

name: DM_VK_TEX_TRACK
meaning: `0` (Android, live: textures made from then on, 1) textures whose storage the CPU may write are filled once instead of tracked and re-uploaded when their pages change

name: DM_VK_TL_HOST
meaning: `1` / `0` (Android, restart only; unset: chosen by a probe at device creation) submissions get fences and the host signals their timeline values instead of the GPU (on for drivers whose zero-timeout queries wait for the GPU: Turnip on KGSL before Mesa e984ef29)

name: DM_VK_TL_POLL
meaning: `1` (Android, live, off) the host's waits for the replay timeline (completion thread, present) read the counter every 0.25 ms instead of blocking in vkWaitSemaphores, to see whether a driver's blocking wait holds its submissions back

name: DM_VK_UBWC
meaning: `0` (Android, live: images made from then on, 1) every colour image is MUTABLE_FORMAT without a format list, as before (any view format; no UBWC compression on Adreno)

name: DM_VK_UB_PEEK
meaning: `=<hex key>[,…]` (Android, restart) logs the uniform buffers (constant buffers) those shaders' draws and dispatches bind from guest memory, as the CPU sees them when recorded (`ub peek`: 16 words as hex and float), to check a pass's parameters; `DM_VK_SB_PEEK_FROM` and `DM_VK_SB_PEEK_LINES` apply

name: DM_VK_UB_PEEK_AT
meaning: `=<word>[,<word>…]` (Android, live) with `DM_VK_UB_PEEK`, the first of the 16 words each line shows (default 0); a list (at most 8) logs one line per window, each counted in `DM_VK_SB_PEEK_LINES`

name: DM_VK_UNPLACE_REMAP
meaning: `1` (Android, experiment, off): giving back a memory pool maps its Vulkan memory again where the driver likes before moving the anonymous pages in, and frees it after them, to find out whether the Adreno driver's vkFreeMemory then leaves the guest range alone (no hole between the free and the move); a `[RED]` line says when it does not (the pool's bytes are then lost). Needs a phone test before any default

name: DM_VK_UPLOAD_BATCH
meaning: `=0` (Android, live, default 1) records a new image's first content into the submission being recorded instead of an upload batch whose staging retires on its own completion (docs/reference/memory.md)

name: DM_VK_UPLOAD_BATCH_MB
meaning: `=<MiB>` (Android, live, 64) the staging an upload batch takes before it goes to the queue

name: DM_VK_UPLOAD_INFLIGHT_MB
meaning: `=<MiB>` (Android, live, 256) the batch staging in flight above which the replay thread waits for the oldest upload batch

name: DM_VK_UPLOAD_MT
meaning: `=<n>` (Android, live, 3) helper threads (`vk-upload`) deswizzle big block-linear texture uploads with the replay thread, in runs of block rows; `0` the replay thread only

name: DM_VK_UPLOAD_MT_MIN
meaning: `=<bytes>` (Android, live, 262144) the smallest texture upload `DM_VK_UPLOAD_MT` spreads over the helper threads

name: DM_VK_VALIDATE
meaning: `1` (Android, restart) turns on the Khronos validation layer when it is installed

name: DM_VK_VB_FILTER
meaning: (Android, live, on) vertex buffers (consecutive slots in one call), the vertex input state and the index buffer are bound only when they change in the command buffer; `0` every slot every draw

name: DM_VK_VIEW_LEARN
meaning: (Android, on) a texture of another format over a live image's memory, or a view in a format the image's list lacks, is learned (format, other format, size) and kept in `$DM_TEMP/vk_view_formats.txt`; images of that format and size made from then on take the other format in their format list (`MUTABLE_FORMAT`, no UBWC for them) and are shared. Until then the texture gets its own image. `0` learns and reads nothing (such textures always get their own image)

name: DM_VK_VIN_SKIP
meaning: `0` (Android, live: the next submission, 1) the vertex input descriptions are built and the vertex buffers bound (and compared) at every draw instead of being kept while the vertex shader, the attribute / stream / buffer records and the placed segments stay the same

name: DM_VK_WORKER
meaning: `0` (Android, restart, on) submissions and presents are replayed inline on the game's thread instead of on the replay worker thread

name: DM_VK_WORKER_FRAMES
meaning: `=<n>` (Android, restart, default 1) the replay worker may be at most n presents behind the game

name: DM_VK_XP_SCISSOR
meaning: `=<px>` (Android, live, 0 = off) an experiment with a wrong picture: every draw's scissor is cut to px x px pixels, to split a pass's GPU time into per-pixel and per-draw work

name: DM_VK_XP_TS
meaning: `=<mask>` (Android, live, 0 = off) an experiment: a bottom-of-pipe timestamp (on Turnip a wait for idle) after a pass end's barrier (1), at an upload batch's end (2), before a depth pass begins (4), after every other full barrier (8) ([rendering.md](reference/rendering.md#turnip-hangs-in-the-first-3d-frame-of-a-cold-run))

name: DM_VK_XP_TS_SEL
meaning: `=<mask>` (Android, live, 0) narrows `DM_VK_XP_TS` bit 4: 1 only when the depth image differs from the last depth pass's, 2 only with a depth clear at the begin, 4 only after a depth pass of at least 8192 pixels a side ([rendering.md](reference/rendering.md#turnip-hangs-in-the-first-3d-frame-of-a-cold-run))

name: DM_VK_ZEROLOG
meaning: `=<n>` (Android): the first n textures made as zero images whose storage holds data at their first use (virtual pools left out), with their description, pool flags and whether the first use was a sample (`vka_tex.c` `storage_mode`)

name: DM_VK_ZLOG
meaning: `1` (Android, at start, off) with `DM_VK_PARTLOG`, logs each draw of a depth pass of at least `DM_VK_ZLOG_MIN` pixels a side (its depth state, shaders, viewport, scissor) and each such pass's begin (depth serial, format, load or clear) and end, kept barriers, clears and timestamps inside it ([rendering.md](reference/rendering.md#turnip-hangs-in-the-first-3d-frame-of-a-cold-run))

name: DM_VK_ZLOG_LINES
meaning: `=<n>` (Android, at start, 30000) the most lines `DM_VK_ZLOG` writes in a run

name: DM_VK_ZLOG_MIN
meaning: `=<px>` (Android, at start, 4096) the smallest side of a depth pass `DM_VK_ZLOG` logs

name: DM_VK_ZSHARE
meaning: `0` (Android, live: images made from then on, on) every image has memory of its own, as before; on, a large image whose content is the GPU's and that nothing has written yet (dense, single-sampled, not 3D, uncompressed, not linear or a window texture) aliases one zeroed allocation per identical create info and gets memory of its own right before its first write (`vka_tex.c` "Zero-shared images"; the ctl stats' `image memory:` line counts them)

name: DM_VK_ZSHARE_MB
meaning: `=<MiB>` (Android, live, 4) the smallest storage of an image `DM_VK_ZSHARE` shares; `0` turns it off

name: DM_VSYNC_HZ
meaning: `=<Hz>`: rate at which a host thread fires the vi vsync event when the display link does not drive it (default 60)

name: DM_WATCH
meaning: `=<s>` dumps all threads after that many seconds (SIGALRM) and turns on the stall watchdog; off unless set

name: DM_WATCH_SAMPLE
meaning: `=<path>` (Mac): when the stall watchdog fires, samples the process for 1 s with `/usr/bin/sample` and writes the thread stacks to that path

name: DM_WATCH_STALL
meaning: `=<s>`: when the frame loop makes no progress for that long (default 15 with `DM_WATCH`), logs a red line, dumps the threads and exits

name: DM_WINDOW
meaning: When set (to any value, `0` included) opens a Mac window with keyboard and controller input; unset runs headless with the guest on the current thread; the Mac launcher sets it

name: DM_WINDOW_SIZE
meaning: `<width>x<height>` (e.g. `1920x1080`) sets the game's window size, which its render targets scale with, for main builds with a profile `window_fn` row (Mac and Android; the Android launcher's Game resolution sets it); with a `res_levels` row instead, the size caps the game's dynamic resolution (its level lists start at the largest level that fits); unset, empty or `original` = the game's own size

name: DM_WINDOW_TOP
meaning: `1` (Mac, with `DM_WINDOW`) orders the game window in front without activating it and keeps it above other apps' windows, so a covered window does not slow the run; `regress.py` sets it

name: DM_XBOX_LABELS
meaning: `1` (Android, restart, off) the button prompts are drawn the Xbox way: when the game opens a font archive (`<mount>:/Font/*.bfarc.zs`), the NinDev-HardKey font's A / B and X / Y drawings are swapped in memory (only X / Y with `DM_PAD_LABELLED=2`, none with `DM_PAD_LABELLED=1`); what the buttons do does not change. Game settings › Xbox button label swap sets it

name: DM_XCODE_DERIVED_DATA
meaning: Xcode derived data folder for `build_ipa.sh` (default `$W/build/ios/xcode-dd`); the NSP script points it into the game's build folder

name: DM_XCODE_PROJECT_DIR
meaning: Folder of the per-game Xcode project that `build_ipa.sh --prepare-xcode` makes (default `$W/xcode`); the NSP script sets it

name: DM_XV_FILE
meaning: File where the attachment validity ledger keeps the keys it disabled after a violation, read at the next launch

name: DM_YIELD_BACKOFF
meaning: `0` turns off the yield back-off; `=<cap µs>[:<start µs>]` sets its sleep cap and the run of yields after which it starts (default 250:2000)

name: DM_ZBIC_LIB
meaning: `=<library>` the ZBIC decoder libzbicdec (`dm/third_party/zstd-zbic`) that `dm/tools/nso.py` loads through ctypes for the segments of system 22.0.0+ modules, in place of `libzbicdec.so` on Android and of the zbic package elsewhere; one that does not load is an Error (the tests set it to a build of their own)
